visuals.text: A failing pump causes congestion behind it: lungs on the left, liver, neck veins and legs on the right.

visual.title: NYHA functional class
visual.label: Breathless walking to the toilet
visual.caption: Class is set by how much activity brings on symptoms.

visuals.title: HFrEF: the big 4
visuals.text: Diuretics such as furosemide are added for symptoms. In HFpEF start with empagliflozin plus spironolactone.

visual.title: Ejection fraction
visual.label: EF 30%
visual.caption: Below 35% (or a wide QRS failing therapy) is the cue for cardiac resynchronisation therapy.

nodes: Low BP, poor LV: IV inotropes

glossary.Fluid congestion: Build-up of fluid in tissues and vessels because blood backs up behind a failing heart.
glossary.Tissue perfusion: Blood flow delivering oxygen to the body's tissues.
glossary.Coronary artery disease: Narrowing of the coronary arteries by atheroma.
glossary.Valvular disease: Disease of the heart valves, such as stenosis or regurgitation.
glossary.Fluid overload: Too much fluid in the body, causing oedema and breathlessness.
glossary.Exercise tolerance: How much physical activity someone can do before symptoms stop them.
glossary.Pulmonary congestion: Fluid and blood backing up in the lungs.
glossary.Crackles: Fine popping sounds heard with a stethoscope as fluid-filled airways open.
glossary.Pulmonary oedema: Fluid in the lung tissue and air sacs.
glossary.Pink frothy sputum: Blood-tinged foamy phlegm coughed up in severe pulmonary oedema.
glossary.Cyanosis: Blue colour of skin or lips from low blood oxygen.
glossary.Peripheral oedema: Swelling of the legs or ankles from fluid in the tissues.
glossary.Prognostic: Telling you about the likely outcome.
glossary.COPD: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: long-term airflow limitation, mostly from smoking.
glossary.Mitral regurgitation: Leaky mitral valve letting blood flow back into the left atrium.
glossary.Aortic stenosis: Narrowing of the aortic valve, making the left ventricle work harder.
glossary.Hyperthyroidism: An overactive thyroid gland producing too much thyroid hormone.
glossary.Asymmetric septal hypertrophy: Thickening of the wall between the ventricles more than the rest of the heart, seen in HOCM.
glossary.Diastolic filling: The ventricle filling with blood while it relaxes.
glossary.Negative predictive value: The chance that someone with a negative test truly does not have the disease.
glossary.Alveolar oedema: Fluid filling the air sacs of the lungs.
glossary.Pleural effusion: Fluid collecting between the lung and chest wall.
glossary.Horizontal fissure: The line separating the right upper and middle lung lobes, seen on chest X-ray.
glossary.ACE inhibitor: A drug blocking angiotensin-converting enzyme, lowering blood pressure and protecting the heart, e.g. ramipril.
glossary.Beta-blocker: A drug slowing the heart and blocking adrenaline's effect, e.g. bisoprolol.
glossary.Carvedilol: A beta-blocker used in heart failure.
glossary.Diuretic: A drug that makes the kidneys pass more salt and water.
glossary.Empagliflozin: An SGLT2 inhibitor: makes the kidneys pass glucose and salt.
glossary.Spironolactone: An aldosterone antagonist diuretic that holds on to potassium.
glossary.Eplerenone: An aldosterone antagonist (MRA) with fewer hormonal side effects than spironolactone.
glossary.Aldosterone antagonist: A drug blocking aldosterone, reducing salt and water retention and heart remodelling.
glossary.Iron deficiency: Too little iron in the body to make normal amounts of haemoglobin.
glossary.AKI: Acute kidney injury: a sudden fall in kidney function.
glossary.Gynaecomastia: Enlargement of breast tissue in men.
glossary.Dapagliflozin: An SGLT2 inhibitor used in heart failure, diabetes and kidney disease.
glossary.Cardiac resynchronisation therapy: A pacemaker pacing both ventricles so they contract together.
glossary.Pneumococcal vaccination: A vaccine against Streptococcus pneumoniae, a common cause of pneumonia.
glossary.High-flow oxygen: Oxygen given at a high rate, e.g. 15 L/min through a non-rebreathe mask.
glossary.Systolic BP: The top blood pressure number, the pressure when the heart contracts.
glossary.Hypoxaemic respiratory failure: Low blood oxygen (type 1 respiratory failure) from the lungs not oxygenating blood.
glossary.Hypercapnia: High carbon dioxide in the blood.
glossary.Dobutamine: An IV inotrope that strengthens heart contraction.
glossary.Milrinone: An IV inotrope and vasodilator used in severe heart failure.
glossary.Metabolic demand: How much oxygen and nutrients the body's tissues need.
glossary.Neurohormonal activation: Switching on of nerve and hormone systems, like RAAS and adrenaline, to support blood pressure.
glossary.Sympathetic nervous system: The fight-or-flight nerves that speed up the heart and narrow vessels.
glossary.Systolic contractility: How strongly the heart muscle squeezes.
glossary.Stroke volume: The volume of blood pumped out with each heartbeat.
glossary.Filling pressures: The pressures in the heart chambers as they fill with blood.
glossary.Transudation: Fluid leaking out of vessels because of pressure, not inflammation.
glossary.Interstitium: The tissue spaces between cells, here around the lung air sacs.
glossary.Hydrostatic pressure: The pushing pressure of fluid inside a vessel.
glossary.Systemic capillaries: The tiny vessels supplying the body's organs, not the lungs.
glossary.ARBs: Angiotensin receptor blockers, e.g. losartan, used when ACE inhibitors cause cough.
glossary.Angiotensin II: A hormone that narrows vessels, retains salt and drives harmful heart remodelling.
